newsitem.title: DUBAI: TENNIS-IVANISEVIC LABOURS BEFORE BEATING ULIHRACH.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-IVANISEVIC LABOURS BEFORE BEATING ULIHRACH.

text.p: Defending champion and top seed Goran Ivanisevic shook off a determined challenge from Bohdan Ulihrach before winning through to the quarter-finals of the $1 million Dubai Open on Thursday.
The Croatian, frustrated by long rallies, had a penalty point for racket abuse deducted before scrambling home to an unimpressive 7-6 6-4 victory.

Ivanisevic, ranked second in the world, struggled to find the usual incisive touch that won him five ATP tour events last year. But as the match wore on, he gradually rediscovered his form to beat the 38th ranked Czech Republic player.
Neither managed a service break in the first set which Ivanisevic won 10-8 on the tie-break.
They exchanged early breaks in the second before Ivanisevic made the decisive break in the eighth game.
Former champion Wayne Ferreira also survived a tough match against veteran Pat Cash before clinching the tension filled 3-6 6-2 7-5 clash.
The South African, seeded fourth, looked headed for a surprise defeat as the Australian wild card raced to a quick 5-0 lead in the first set.
But then Cash's service control deserted him and although he held on to take the first set allowed Ferreira, winner of the 1995 event here, to bounce back.
The vital turnaround came when a backhand down the line from Ferreira clipped the top of the net and fell in to give the fourth seed a break for a 3-1 lead in the second set.
The final set was closer, with many games going to deuce.
"Two mis-hits in the last set killed my chances," Cash said.
"I needed to win three or four matches to get into the groove," the former Wimbledon champion said. "But then things sometimes don't go your way."

Ferreira admitted: "In the first set I played awful, but I was a little more consistent after that. Mentally, it was tough to get going today, but I am glad I was able to overcome that and played decent tennis in the second and third sets."
Current Wimbledon Champion Richard Krajicek continued his good form, beating Javier Sanchez 6-3 6-2.

Playing his first tournament since undergoing knee surgery in December, the Dutchman appeared far less tentative than during his first round match against India's Leander Paes and won in under an hour.

"It was much better today," said third seeded Krajicek. "I was much more aggressive and positive. This morning I woke up and for the first time my knees didn't hurt after a match. Yesterday I wasn't moving well, but today it was 100 percent better."
